title: All Options: How to Upgrade to Business Class on Jetstar
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
New Jetstar Boeing 787 Business Class seats. Photo: Jetstar.
Getting an upgrade to Jetstar Business Class is now easier than ever. Jetstar has launched two new ways to move up front from Economy: bidding for a seat with BidCash, or using Qantas Points to request a Jetstar Classic Upgrade.
With Jetstar refitting its Boeing 787s with more than twice as many Business Class seats, your chances of scoring an upgrade are only getting better.
Here is how each option works, what it costs and which one offers the best value.
Which Jetstar flights can you upgrade?
Jetstar only operates a Business Class cabin on its wide-body Boeing 787 aircraft. These operate flights from Australia to Singapore, Seoul, Colombo, Phuket, Osaka and Ho Chi Minh City. Jetstar’s Airbus A320 and A321neo aircraft don’t have a Business Class cabin.
Jetstar Boeing 787. Photo: Jetstar.
Jetstar is in the process of refitting all 11 of its 787s with a 44-seat Business Class cabin (up from 21 seats), plus Wi-Fi. The first refitted aircraft entered service in April 2026, and more seats up front should mean better odds of an upgrade.
Check how you booked
The biggest catch when it comes to Jetstar upgrades is how you booked your flight. Jetstar flights booked on qantas.com (including ones with a Qantas (QF) flight number) are not currently eligible for any of its upgrade options. Bookings made through a travel agent or another website may be eligible, as long as the booking can be retrieved on the upgrade page. If you want the best chance of upgrading, book directly on the Jetstar website.
Jetstar now offers multiple upgrade options. Screenshot from Jetstar website.
Option 1: Bid for an upgrade with BidCash
BidCash launched in March 2026. It works much like Qantas Bid Now and Virgin Australia’s UpgradeMe systems. You name your price, and Jetstar decides whether to accept it.
Despite the name, you don’t have to pay entirely in cash. You can pay for a BidCash bid with cash only, or with Points Plus Pay, which combines Qantas Points and cash.
Here is how it works:
Eligible passengers receive an email invitation to bid in the days before their flight. You can also check your booking on the Jetstar Business Class upgrades page without waiting for an email.
Use the slider to choose your bid. Minimum and maximum amounts vary by route. At launch, bids on Melbourne to Ho Chi Minh City started at $180 per person. AFF member moa999 reported a range of $210-800 on Sydney to Seoul, with a “recommended” bid of $625.
You enter your card details when you bid, but you are only charged if the upgrade goes through.
You can raise, lower or cancel your bid until four hours before departure, or until Jetstar tells you the outcome.
Jetstar can confirm the result any time up to four hours before departure. If you are successful, you will receive a new itinerary by email.
The BidCash slider for a Sydney to Seoul flight, with bids from $210-800. Screenshot: AFF member moa999
Don’t check in until you have heard back. Jetstar says checking in before your upgrade is confirmed makes the upgrade request invalid.
Paying for your bid with Points Plus Pay
Since June 2026, Qantas Frequent Flyer members can cover part of a BidCash bid with Qantas Points. Select Points Plus Pay on the bidding page, log in to your Qantas Frequent Flyer account and use a second slider to split your bid between points and cash.
Points can cover up to 80% of the bid. In practice, members have found that the points portion is capped at 80% of the minimum bid, even if you bid higher.
The value is poor. On Sydney to Seoul, AFF member moa999 found that 31,000 Qantas Points offset just $164 of the bid. That is about 0.53 cents per point, which is well below what you would get from most Classic Flight Rewards.
On an $800 bid, 31,000 Qantas Points reduces the cash amount by just $164. Screenshot: AFF member moa999
Option 2: Request a Jetstar Classic Upgrade
This is the option that many Qantas Frequent Flyers have been waiting for. Launched in September 2026, Jetstar Classic Upgrades work much like Qantas Classic Upgrade rewards. You request an upgrade for a fixed number of Qantas Points, set by route, rather than placing a bid.
Examples at launch include:
Melbourne to Singapore: 37,000 Qantas Points
Sydney to Osaka: 45,300 Qantas Points
These prices are one way, per person. You will see the exact price for your flight when you enter your booking on the upgrade page.
Here are the key rules:
Jetstar generally processes requests in the order they are submitted. Unlike Qantas, there is no mention of priority based on Frequent Flyer status.
Points are only deducted if the upgrade is successful.
You can submit a request without enough points, but you will need the full amount in your account when the upgrade is processed.
As with BidCash, you can change or cancel your request until four hours before departure, and you shouldn’t check in until you have heard back.
Can you bid and request a Classic Upgrade at the same time?
Yes! You can place a BidCash offer and a Classic Upgrade request on the same flight. Jetstar processes the Classic Upgrade first. If it is accepted, your BidCash offer is cancelled automatically.
What you get (and don’t get) when you upgrade
A successful upgrade through either BidCash or a Classic Upgrade includes:
Priority boarding
A recliner seat with extra legroom
Meals, selected wines and extra snacks
30kg of checked baggage and two small carry-on items
Wi-Fi or in-flight entertainment where available
A comfort pack
Steamed market fish with rice, sourdough and a side salad in Jetstar Business Class. Photo: Arun AA
You won’t get lounge access unless you already have it through Qantas Frequent Flyer status or another lounge membership. You also won’t get the flexibility of a Business Class fare, as your original Economy fare rules still apply. This also means, if eligible, you will earn Qantas Points and status credits under the original Economy fare rules.
The fine print
You lose your extras. Anything you paid for on the upgraded flight, such as seat selection or a baggage add-on, is forfeited and not refunded.
Changes cancel the upgrade. If you change an upgraded flight, you lose the upgrade and the amount you paid for it. Your original fare rules apply to the change.
Delays and cancellations. If Jetstar delays or cancels your flight, the upgrade is cancelled and refunded, and you go back to your original fare.
Connecting flights. If only one leg of a connecting trip is upgraded, you will get the Business Class baggage allowance for the connecting leg too. For example, if you are flying from Melbourne to Bangkok via Brisbane, the Melbourne-Brisbane leg also gets 30kg. This doesn’t apply to a separate return flight, though.
Which upgrade option is best?
It depends on what you have more of. If you have lots of points to spare, request a Jetstar Classic Upgrade. If you prefer to save your points for a more aspirational redemption, place a BidCash bid near the minimum and pay with cash only. And, if you want the best odds, do both! Just remember to cancel your other bid.
We would skip paying for a BidCash bid with Points Plus Pay as you only get about half a cent per point!
Have you been upgraded on Jetstar? Tell us how much you bid, or how many points your Jetstar Classic Upgrade cost, on the Australian Frequent Flyer (AFF) forum!
